title: Complex Numbers

sections.heading: 1. Cartesian, Polar & Exponential Forms
sections.proseLatex: A complex number $Z = x + iy$ has modulus $|Z| = \sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ and argument $\arg Z = \tan^{-1}(y/x)$.

keyFormulas.label: Modulus & Argument
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Convert between Cartesian and polar forms.

sections.heading: 2. Cube Roots of Unity & De Moivre
sections.proseLatex: The cube roots of unity are $1, \omega, \omega^2$ where $\omega = e^{2\pi i/3}$. They satisfy $1 + \omega + \omega^2 = 0$.

keyFormulas.label: De Moivre's Theorem
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Compute powers and roots of complex numbers.

wbjeebTraps: Reciprocal polynomials: if coefficients are symmetric, roots come in reciprocal pairs.
